messages:
juan_support: FYI customer ACCT-9812 (eu-west-1, Dedicated) reporting sudden latency spikes and unexpected billing to hosted. p50 ~250ms -> spikes to 900-1200ms; billing shows ~4.6k tokens charged to hosted in last 40m. They say this started when their TTL refresh job for region pin ran. Logs and repro below.

juan_support: Relevant excerpt from routing log (sanitized):
```json
{"ts":"2026-03-16T18:10:12Z","account":"ACCT-9812","req_id":"r-7f3a","route_decision":{"type":"dedicated_pin","pin_state":"expired","action":"fallback","fallback_target":"hosted","reason":"compatibility_check_pass","selected_region":"us-east-1"}}
```

juan_support: Repro curl (customer):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" \
  -H "X-Redwood-Account: ACCT-9812" \
  -H "X-Redwood-Preferred-Region: eu-west-1" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?model=redwood-13b
```

alice: looking. can you paste the raw route_decision payload for a few traces where billing went to hosted?

juan_support: pasted two more (traces truncated):
```json
{"ts":"2026-03-16T18:10:13Z","req_id":"r-7f3b","route_decision":{"pin_check":"miss","cache_hit":false,"fallback_hosted":true,"fallback_reason":"variant_compatibility","selected_region":"us-east-1"},"billing_target":"hosted"}
{"ts":"2026-03-16T18:10:15Z","req_id":"r-7f9c","route_decision":{"pin_check":"present","pin_ttl_remaining":0.9,"cache_stale":true,"fallback_hosted":false,"selected_region":"eu-west-1"},"billing_target":"dedicated"}
```

carla_ops: looks like a TTL race + routing-cache inconsistency. pin was removed then re-added very quickly during the TTL refresh; some requests observed the transient missing state and routed to hosted. the weird bit is compatibility check allowed a hosted variant in a different region (us-east-1) even though X-Redwood-Preferred-Region was eu-west-1. fallback heuristics should respect region affinity.

brian_m: confirmed via routing_events: we saw ~320 routing decisions for ACCT-9812 between 18:09:58 and 18:11:00. Query I ran: 
```
SELECT ts, req_id, route_type, selected_region, billing_target, pin_state
FROM routing_events
WHERE account = 'ACCT-9812' AND ts BETWEEN '2026-03-16T18:09:50Z' AND '2026-03-16T18:11:10Z'
ORDER BY ts;
```

brian_m: results show pin_deleted at 18:10:12.278, pin_create at 18:10:14.112. requests between those timestamps mostly fell back to hosted and selected us-east-1 due to a placement heuristic that preferred lower-cost hosted variants without region gating.

robin_sre: we should treat short pin lapses (<30s) as refresh race and prefer same-region hosted backfill (or better: avoid cross-region hosted backfill entirely if request headers indicate region preference). simple change: require fallback_hosted to match X-Redwood-Preferred-Region unless explicitly allowed.

juan_support: customer provided a timeline: their TTL refresh script does remove+recreate pin on rotation, it briefly unpins for ~1.8s while K/V rotates. so this is reproducible. steps: 1) create pin; 2) run rotation that deletes then re-adds pin; 3) spike requests during gap -> observe hosted billing.

alice: thanks. can eng-runtime add a guard to routing: if account had a pin deletion event within last 30s do not allow cross-region hosted selection — instead either queue briefly or pick same-region hosted variant. i'll take a canary patch.

deploy-bot: canary deploy started: commit abc1234 -> eng-runtime/eu-west-1 at 2026-03-16T18:25:00Z (1790123900).

robin_sre: monitoring dashboards: watch routing_mismatch_rate, hosted_billing_rate_by_account, p95_latency for ACCT-9812. set alert if hosted_billing_rate > 2% for >5m.

brian_m: ran immediate mitigation via infra: pinned routing-cache TTL extension for ACCT-9812 to 12s for the rebind window, reduced observed hosted fallthroughs to near zero.

juan_support: i relayed to customer. they replayed traffic and confirmed p95 dropped back to ~320ms and no additional hosted billing spikes seen. customer asked for a billing credit for the ~4.6k tokens billed to hosted. recommend partial credit.

alice: filing follow-up issue: runtime-1239. long-term fix: (1) require region-aware fallback, (2) tighten pin refresh API so rotation can rebind without delete, (3) add end-to-end test that simulates pin rotation.

juan_support: customer happy with mitigation + credit plan. closing loop; will wait for final deploy and retro. :thumbsup:

carla_ops: note for postmortem: include sample trace ids r-7f3a r-7f3b r-7f9c and the SQL extract. attach to incident later.

alice: rolling the canary to prod region set now (commit abc1234 -> all eu regions). will update when done.

deploy-bot: rollout complete for commit abc1234 at 2026-03-16T18:48:43Z (1790124123).

juan_support: thanks everyone. tagging this thread for retro and billing ops follow-up.
